target.hypothetical_carrier: integral Cartier divisor C in |D_l| with normalization genus 1 and retained packet

construction.global_generation: O_S(H) is basepoint-free canonical morphism; hence V tensor O_S -> i_*A is surjective
construction.local_freeness: C is Cartier and A is invertible on C; locally the quotient is R/(f), so the kernel of a surjection R^7 -> R/(f) is free of rank 7

discriminant.consequence: E cannot be slope-semistable with respect to an ample polarization; it has a nontrivial Harder-Narasimhan destabilizing subsheaf

why_promote: The bundle is canonically produced from every hypothetical carrier; no branch-to-product-cover adapter is needed.
The discriminant has a uniform strictly negative sign for every l>=1.
Instability produces new global divisor/sheaf data rather than another counting identity.
The elementary-transform presentation F subset O_S^7 gives extra structure that may constrain destabilizing determinants.

questions: Let G be the maximal destabilizing subsheaf of F or E. Determine rank and determinant inequalities from F subset O_S^7 and mu_H.
Use the exact Picard lattice and known zero-quartic/rank-3-fibration intersections to test whether any destabilizing determinant class can exist.
Check whether the support-hyperplane section forces a specific elementary-transform subobject, which could identify rather than merely bound the HN class.

external_theorem: Bogomolov-Gieseker inequality for slope-semistable torsion-free sheaves on a smooth projective surface in characteristic zero

second_scan_result.setup: For F subset O_S^7, a saturated destabilizing subsheaf G of rank r has det G=O(-B) with B effective and -H.B/r > -16*l, i.e. H.B < 16*l*r.

exact_witness_family.known_curve_pairings: H has nonnegative intersections with retained effective test curves and is itself effective/canonical

supported_exceptional_restriction.statement: On a supported exceptional E_i, H|E_i is trivial and the elementary transform restricts as O_E^6 plus O_E(-8*l).
supported_exceptional_restriction.consequence: A determinant condition B.E_i>=0 is compatible with B=H, since H.E_i=0.

decision.reason: Bogomolov instability is genuine, but slope/effectivity/intersection inequalities alone leave an explicit determinant witness B=H at rank 2 for every l. Any continuation must use the actual embedding G->F/evaluation geometry, not only the Picard cone.
